title: Webview Versions
claims: Tauri uses WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS and WebKitGTK on Linux.
Platform WebView versions depend on the installed platform/runtime and must be recorded in qualification.
notes: Official moving Tauri v2 documentation fetched; not an installed support or footprint result. Do not adopt legacy OS support wording as Splyce's support policy. License anchors also fetched: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/tauri/tauri-v2.0.0/LICENSE_MIT and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/tauri/tauri-v2.0.0/LICENSE_APACHE-2.0. These tags anchor license inspection only, not implementation pins.

tool: Tauri external binary and Node sidecar packaging
title: Embedding External Binaries
claims: Tauri can bundle external binaries with target-specific naming and launch an owned sidecar.
Shell-plugin execution requires configured permissions; packaging a binary alone does not grant frontend execution authority.
notes: Also fetched https://v2.tauri.app/learn/sidecar-nodejs/ as the official Node packaging example. Neither example qualifies Pi's dynamic loading/native dependencies, descendant cleanup or Node runtime compatibility. Proposed delivery includes pinned Node and Pi resources rather than requiring ambient Node or assuming Bun.

title: Capabilities and security boundaries
claims: Capabilities enable and constrain frontend exposure to core/plugin APIs with window-associated permissions.
The documented boundary does not protect against malicious Rust, incorrect command scope checks or overly broad configuration.
notes: Proposed narrow Rust commands must still validate every request and recheck effect grants in Pi; Tauri capabilities do not sandbox trusted in-process Pi extensions. No adversarial runtime test executed.

title: WebDriver: embedded service and native driver routes
claims: The accessed guide documents @wdio/tauri-service with embedded WebDriver support on Windows, Linux and macOS.
Direct tauri-driver desktop support is Windows and Linux; the guide directs macOS to embedded service or another qualified route.
Renderer-only browser mode can mock invoke calls and does not exercise an installed Tauri binary.
notes: Important distinction from older macOS automation limitations. Test-only embedded plugins must not ship in production. Screen readers, real native dialogs, process cleanup and actual release installation still need individual platform tests; n=0.

title: Windows Installer: WebView2 provisioning modes
claims: The guide distinguishes downloadable/embedded bootstrapper, offline installer and fixed WebView2 runtime modes.
Offline or fixed-runtime delivery adds runtime payload; a bootstrapper is not a dependency-complete offline installation.
notes: Vendor example byte counts are intentionally not repeated as Splyce measurements. Actual app, Node, Pi, WebView and installed dependency costs remain n=0; Linux/macOS delivery must qualify their own package/runtime closures.

title: Updater: signed artifacts and platform targets
claims: Updater metadata identifies target artifacts and signatures; artifact signing is part of the documented updater path.
Update check and installation use configured endpoints and application APIs.
notes: Explicit checks, no unsolicited network activity, interruption recovery and compatible app/Node/Pi updates are proposed Splyce requirements, not guarantees supplied by the plugin. Manual verified installers suffice initially; no update operation tested.

title: Process Model
claims: Electron separates its privileged Node main process from window renderer processes and supports Node utility processes.
An owned utility process is a potential Pi engine host, subject to Node compatibility and lifecycle tests.
notes: Also fetched official https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/tutorial-prerequisites establishing bundled Chromium/Node and https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security/ for context isolation/sandbox boundaries. MIT license anchor fetched at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v33.0.0/LICENSE; v33.0.0 is not a selected/current implementation version. No size or performance comparison measured.

title: Compiler warnings: accessibility diagnostics
claims: Svelte exposes compiler diagnostics for labels, keyboard interactions, roles, focus and other accessibility markup concerns.
These diagnostics are a static gate; the proposed app still requires actual keyboard and screen-reader verification.
notes: Svelte 5/TypeScript static frontend is a design choice, not a measured performance winner. MIT text fetched at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sveltejs/svelte/svelte%405.0.0/LICENSE.md; this is a license inspection anchor, not a selected/current release.

title: Slint getting started and license choices
claims: Slint offers a Rust application integration route.
The official page distinguishes GPLv3, Community and commercial licensing paths; Slint cannot be assumed MIT.
notes: This research does not select a Slint distribution/license or establish AGPL compatibility of an actual combined package. Native accessibility, renderer footprint and Node/Pi lifecycle remain untested.

title: egui official repository
claims: egui is an immediate-mode Rust GUI with native/web integration routes.
The accessed README documents optional AccessKit integration and platform-specific accessibility scope.
notes: Moving README, not a qualified source pin. Also fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emilk/egui/0.29.1/LICENSE-MIT as a license anchor only. Text selection, IME, screen-reader behavior, Linux accessibility and idle CPU need tests; do not infer unsupported behavior merely from documentation silence.

title: Pi createAgentSession SDK inputs and result

The result includes extensionsResult and modelFallbackMessage; a GUI must qualify extension binding and reject silent model fallback under Splyce policy.
notes: Direct public pinned SDK fetched. Repository Pi source contracts supply the wider hook/lifecycle/branch audit; this record is source observation, not installed Pi or SDK/RPC parity testing.

title: Pi coding-agent package runtime and license manifest

Node runtime packaging and the complete installed Pi dependency/resource closure require qualification; no Bun compatibility is inferred.
notes: Manifest at the same immutable source revision as DESK-11. Source identity does not establish registry publication, actual installed behavior, dynamic-plugin packaging or measured resource use.

title: Svelte overview
claims: Svelte compiles declarative HTML/CSS/JavaScript components and documents TypeScript component syntax.
SvelteKit is a companion full-stack framework, distinct from using Svelte components for a static desktop UI.
notes: Svelte 5 is the locked frontend family with Vite static assets and scoped CSS/custom-property tokens. No SSR server is needed by the product contract. No measured footprint or universal framework superiority follows from this choice.

title: Fine-grained reactivity
claims: Solid documents signals and tracked computations for targeted reactive updates.
notes: Credible streaming-UI alternative; mechanism is not a measured whole-app cost advantage over Svelte. No Solid build, installed test or dependency addition performed.

title: Thinking in React
claims: React documents component hierarchy, explicit ownership of state and one-way data flow.
notes: Candidate evaluated for the same desktop screen/state contract; not selected. No claim that React cannot satisfy the product or is universally slower/larger.

notes: Template availability supports the bounded framework comparison; no scaffold/install was run. Selected Svelte/Vite assets are packaged locally with no Express or SvelteKit SSR server.

title: Monaco Editor official repository and FAQ

Vendor assertions about worker overhead are not local measurements. Monaco is the user-selected separately installed editor; local ESM assets/workers, no CDN. Base contains zero editor/worker payload and retains simple text/diff views; LSP remains separately selected. CodeMirror is a comparator only.
